capture.finding.cookieNoHttpOnly.title: Cookie without HttpOnly
capture.finding.cookieNoHttpOnly.detail: Cookie "{name}" from {host} is readable by JavaScript, so an XSS bug can steal it. Add the HttpOnly attribute.
capture.finding.cookieNoSecure.title: Cookie without Secure
capture.finding.cookieNoSecure.detail: Cookie "{name}" from {host} can also be sent over plain HTTP. Add the Secure attribute.
capture.finding.cookieNoSameSite.title: Cookie without SameSite
capture.finding.cookieNoSameSite.detail: Cookie "{name}" from {host} has no SameSite attribute, so the browser default applies and cross-site request protection is not explicit.
capture.finding.cookieSameSiteNoneInsecu: Cookie "{name}" from {host} uses SameSite=None but is not Secure; modern browsers reject it and it is exposed cross-site over HTTP.
capture.finding.missingCsp.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
capture.finding.missingCsp.detail: The page from {host} sets no CSP, so nothing limits injected scripts or external resources.
capture.finding.missingHsts.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security
capture.finding.missingHsts.detail: {host} does not send HSTS, so a first request or downgrade attack can fall back to HTTP.
capture.finding.missingXcto.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
capture.finding.missingXcto.detail: {host} does not send "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff", so browsers may sniff the MIME type.
capture.finding.missingFrameProtection.d: The page from {host} has neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors, so any site can frame it.
capture.finding.missingReferrerPolicy.de: {host} sets no Referrer-Policy, so full URLs may leak in the Referer header.
{host} answers Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Allow-Credentials: true. This is a misconfiguration; check the origin allow-list logic.
capture.finding.corsReflectOrigin.title: CORS reflects the Origin
capture.finding.corsReflectOrigin.detail: {host} echoed the request Origin {origin} (credentials allowed: {credentials}). If it reflects any origin, any site can read responses.
capture.finding.mixedContent.title: Mixed content
capture.finding.mixedContent.detail: An HTTPS page loads a {type} over plain HTTP from {host}; it can be read or tampered with on the network.
capture.finding.credentialsInUrl.title: Secret in URL
capture.finding.credentialsInUrl.detail: The query parameter "{key}" to {host} looks like a credential. URLs end up in logs, history and Referer headers.
capture.finding.userinfoInUrl.title: Credentials in URL userinfo
capture.finding.userinfoInUrl.detail: The URL to {host} embeds the user "{user}" (and possibly a password) before the host name.
capture.finding.jwtAlgNone.title: JWT with alg "none"
capture.finding.jwtAlgNone.detail: A token seen on {host} is unsigned (alg: {alg}); if the server accepts it, anyone can forge tokens.
capture.finding.jwtExpired.title: Expired JWT
capture.finding.jwtExpired.detail: A token seen on {host} has already expired (exp is in the past).
capture.finding.basicAuthOverHttp.title: Basic auth over HTTP
capture.finding.basicAuthOverHttp.detail: Credentials are sent to {host} in clear text (Base64 only) over plain HTTP.
capture.finding.serverVersion.title: Server version disclosed
capture.finding.serverVersion.detail: {host} sends "Server: {value}", which helps attackers pick known exploits.
capture.finding.poweredBy.title: X-Powered-By disclosed
capture.finding.aspnetVersion.title: ASP.NET version disclosed
capture.finding.verboseError.title: Verbose error in response
capture.finding.verboseError.detail: A response from {host} contains a stack trace or database error ({pattern}) that leaks internals.
capture.finding.directoryListing.title: Directory listing enabled
capture.finding.directoryListing.detail: {host} returns an "Index of /" page that exposes file names.
capture.finding.cacheNoStore.title: Sensitive response may be cached
capture.finding.cacheNoStore.detail: A response from {host} sets cookies or answers an authenticated request without Cache-Control: no-store.

capture.sec.owasp.A02.name: Cryptographic Failures
capture.sec.owasp.A03.name: Injection
capture.sec.owasp.A04.name: Insecure Design
capture.sec.owasp.A05.name: Security Misconfiguration
capture.sec.owasp.A06.name: Vulnerable & Outdated Components
capture.sec.owasp.A07.name: Identification & Authentication Failures
capture.sec.owasp.A08.name: Software & Data Integrity Failures
capture.sec.owasp.A09.name: Security Logging & Monitoring Failures

capture.sec.guide.A01: Change object ids in the path/query (see the IDOR payload) and check whether another user's data is returned.
capture.sec.guide.A02: Review the findings for plain HTTP, missing HSTS and secrets in URLs — passive analysis is done; the rest needs manual review.
capture.sec.guide.A03: Send the SQLi / XSS / command payloads through the Repeater and compare responses.
capture.sec.guide.A04: Design review: check rate limits, abuse cases and business logic — cannot be detected passively.
capture.sec.guide.A05: Review the security headers, CORS and verbose errors in the findings.
capture.sec.guide.A06: Match the detected technology versions below against NVD / Exploit-DB.
capture.sec.guide.A07: Check session cookies (Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite) and try the JWT payloads in the Repeater.
capture.sec.guide.A08: Check for unsigned updates or untrusted data — a manual review is required.
capture.sec.guide.A09: Logging/monitoring cannot be verified from traffic — review the server side manually.
capture.sec.guide.A10: Look for parameters that take a URL (webhooks, fetch, image proxies) and try pointing them at internal hosts.
capture.sec.tech.title: Detected technologies
capture.sec.tech.empty: No technology fingerprinted from the captured responses.
capture.sec.tech.col.name: Technology
capture.sec.nvd.hint: Fetch CVEs from NVD for this technology (network call, runs only when you click)
capture.sec.nvd.note: Queries the public NVD API (services.nvd.nist.gov). Runs only when you click — nothing is sent automatically.
capture.sec.nvd.empty: No CVE found for this keyword.
capture.sec.payload.title: Payloads
capture.sec.payload.hint: Starting points for manual testing — nothing is sent automatically. Send to Repeater and adjust to the target.
capture.sec.payload.sqli-error.d: Inject ' OR '1'='1 into a query parameter and compare the response.
capture.sec.payload.sqli-error-extract.d: MySQL error-based extraction — the DBMS version appears in the error.
capture.sec.payload.sqli-time.d: SLEEP(3) — a response delayed ~3s indicates injection.
capture.sec.payload.xss-svg.d: Breaks out of an attribute and runs onload — check whether it reflects unencoded.
capture.sec.payload.ssti-basic.d: Template injection probe — look for 49 in the response.
capture.sec.payload.ssti-el.d: Expression Language variant — look for 49 in the response.
capture.sec.payload.cmd-semi.d: Appends a shell command — look for uid= in the response.
capture.sec.payload.cmd-pipe.d: Pipes into a shell command — look for a username in the response.
capture.sec.payload.xxe.d: Paste as the XML request body — reads /etc/passwd if the parser resolves entities.
capture.sec.payload.traversal.d: ../../../etc/passwd — look for root:x: in the response.
capture.sec.payload.traversal-escape.d: Doubled separators that survive naive ../ stripping.
capture.sec.payload.idor.d: Change the object id in the path/query and check whether another user's data is returned.
capture.sec.payload.jwt-alg-none.d: Unsigned JWT template — replace the payload claims and send it as a Bearer token.
capture.sec.payload.jwt-kid.d: kid: ../../dev/null — sign with an empty secret to test kid path injection.
capture.sec.payload.origin-reflect.d: Send Origin: https://evil.example and check whether ACAO echoes it.
capture.sec.payload.crlf.d: %0d%0aX-Injected:1 — check whether the response gains an X-Injected header.
capture.sec.scan.title: Security scan
capture.sec.scan.hint: Active testing replays mutated requests to the target host — only run on systems you are authorized to test. Runs only when you click.
capture.sec.scan.goHint: Replay probe requests against the target (user-initiated, confirm first)
capture.sec.scan.clean: Scanned {n} probes against {hosts} — no active findings.
capture.sec.scan.confirmDesc: This sends mutated test requests (SQLi, XSS, traversal…) to {host}. Only continue if you are authorized to test this system.
capture.sec.agent.hint: Create a new chat session and send these findings for analysis
capture.sec.agent.sent: Findings sent to a new agent session
capture.sec.scan.blocked: Stopped early: {n} consecutive transport errors (likely WAF/CDN blocking or network loss).
capture.sec.probe.empty: Nothing scanned yet — hit "Scan" to run the challenge scenarios.
